_comment: The order Elasticsearch requires, not a preference. A composed index
template is rejected at PUT time when composed_of names a component that
does not exist yet, so components come first. An ILM policy named by a
template is NOT checked at PUT time: get that order wrong and the template
installs cleanly, then every index it creates sits with no lifecycle until
someone looks. So policies go first too.
The last step is the one people forget. A rollover alias has to exist
before the first write, and it has to be created with is_write_index true,
because an alias pointing at more than one index refuses writes and the
error arrives at the producer rather than here.
